| | |

| **Software version** | 4.0.2 |
| **Spec revision** | v003 (supersedes v002) |
| **Date** | 2026-07-22 |
| **Status** | Implemented |

This revision extends v002 with a second round of issues: the flickering icon
column, the reappearing Welcome dialog, and two latent state bugs uncovered
while diagnosing them. Root causes were verified by a multi-agent
investigation (three independent analysis lenses, each claim adversarially
re-checked against the code).

## The "Actions" column, explained

The first table column after the checkbox holds two per-row buttons — **↗
Switch to Tab** and **× Close Tab**. They are rendered with `opacity: 0` and
only become visible when the row is hovered or selected, which is why the
column usually looks empty. The icon users see flickering is **not** in the
Actions column: it is the favicon column, the narrow unlabeled column between
Actions and Tab Name.

## Issue 5 — Continuous icon flicker while idle

**Primary cause (confirmed).** Rows whose favicon could not load fell back to
`https://via.placeholder.com/16?text=?` via an `onError` handler that
re-assigned `img.src`. That domain is dead (TLS connections fail). Per the
HTML spec, assigning `src` — even the same value — restarts image fetching,
so each failure re-fired `onError`, which re-assigned `src`, forever: an
infinite error/retry loop repainting the 16 px icon (blank ↔ broken-glyph)
several times a second, on every affected row at once, with a continuous
stream of doomed network requests. With 174 tabs, several rows were always
looping. The same defect existed in `PreviewPanel` and the (unused)
`TabCard`.

**Amplifier (confirmed).** The dashboard subscribes to eight `chrome.tabs`/
`chrome.windows` events with a 200 ms debounce and reloads the full window
snapshot on each. Background tabs (Gmail unread counts, YouTube, Memory
Saver discards) fire these continuously, so the table re-rendered every few
hundred milliseconds even when idle. React only commits real DOM changes for
rows whose data changed — but the events themselves supply such changes
(title strings, tabs cycling through reload transiently reporting **no**
favicon), so icons flipped between image and fallback as tabs slept and woke.

**Fixes.**

- New `components/Favicon.tsx`: renders the tab icon with a **local** Globe
  glyph fallback (no network). A `failed` flag latches on error and resets
  only when the URL actually changes — a loop is structurally impossible.
  Fixed 16 px box, so no width wobble. Replaces the broken `<img onError>`
  pattern in `TabListView` and `PreviewPanel`; the unused `TabCard.tsx`
  (same defect) was deleted.
- `services/tabService.ts` keeps a `lastKnownFavicons` map (tab id → last
  non-empty `favIconUrl`), so tabs mid-reload keep their icon instead of
  flashing the fallback.
- `loadTabs` now computes a JSON signature of the fresh window snapshot and
  **skips all state updates when nothing changed**, so display-irrelevant
  events (audible/muted/loading churn) no longer re-render 174 rows.

## Issue 6 — Welcome dialog reappears after being dismissed

**Cause (confirmed).** The **X** button and "Got it" both close the dialog
passing the "Don't show this again" checkbox state (default *unchecked*), so
plain dismissal never persists `hasSeenOnboarding`. The first-run check ran
inside `loadTabs`, which re-runs on **every** chrome tab event — and
browsing previews generates a stream of them (waking/reloading a discarded
tab fires `onUpdated` several times). Result: dismiss with X, wake a few
tabs, dialog pops up again.

**Fix.** A session-scoped guard (`hasAutoShownWelcome` ref): the dialog
auto-shows **at most once per app session**, no matter how it is dismissed.
Semantics now:

- Fresh profile, first launch → dialog shows once.
- Dismissed with X or "Got it" (checkbox unchecked) → stays closed for the
  rest of the session; will show once again next session.
- "Don't show this again" checked → never auto-shows again.
- Help menu → "Show Welcome Screen" still opens it manually at any time.

## Issue 7 (latent) — Stale subscription closure resetting undo history

Found during the flicker investigation. The mount-time effect captured the
first-render `loadTabs` closure permanently (`[]` deps), so every chrome
event ran with `windows=[]`, `historyIndex=-1`: it blinked the toolbar
refresh spinner, and — worse — took the "first load" branch, **resetting the
window-rename undo/redo history on every event** and rebuilding the name map
(un-persisted in-session names could be reverted).

**Fix.** The subscription now calls the latest `loadTabs` through a ref
(`loadTabsRef`), so event-driven reloads see current state and take the
normal update path. Undo history survives background events.

## Issue 8 (latent) — Unstable `lastAccessed` fallback

`getWindows` mapped `lastAccessed: t.lastAccessed || Date.now()` — tabs
lacking the field were re-stamped with a fresh time on every reload,
churning the default "Last Accessed" sort order. Now falls back to a stable
`0`, displayed as "—" in the table.

## Issue 9 — Adversarial review findings (hardening round)

After the fixes above, an adversarial multi-agent review of the full diff
(three lenses, 21 agents, every finding re-verified against the code)
confirmed nine further defects, all fixed:

1. **Popup layout**: preview-pane-open-by-default would squeeze the ~800 px
   extension *popup* to an unusably narrow table. The pane now defaults open
   only when the viewport is wider than 800 px (full-tab dashboard) and stays
   closed in the popup.
2. **Snapshot-skip side effects**: the manual Refresh button silently did
   nothing when the snapshot was unchanged, and relative "Last Accessed"
   times froze during quiet periods. Refresh now forces a reload
   (`loadTabs(true)`), and the table re-renders once a minute so times keep
   ticking.
3. **Duplicate window names**: after closing a window, the stale in-memory
   name map shadowed the recomputed defaults, yielding two "window2" and no
   "window1". Since every rename path (manual, AI, undo/redo) persists to
   storage, the recomputed defaults + stored customs are now authoritative
   on reload; closed windows are pruned from the map.
4. **Stale favicon after navigation**: the last-known-favicon cache is now
   scoped to the page *origin*, so a tab that navigates from github.com to a
   site with no favicon stops showing GitHub's icon (the mid-reload
   flicker protection, where the origin is unchanged, still works).
5. **Wake button on the wrong tab**: switching tabs while a (up to 15 s)
   wake was in flight let its completion clear the *new* tab's UI, and a
   previous tab's "asleep" flag could briefly mislabel the next tab. Per-tab
   flags are reset on every fetch, and wake completion is keyed to the tab
   it started for.
6. **Crash on URL-less tabs**: `new URL('')` for a tab still pending its
   first navigation threw during render, white-screening the app (no error
   boundary). The PreviewPanel now guards hostname parsing like the table
   already did.
7. **CSV export** printed 12/31/1969 for tabs with the new stable
   `lastAccessed: 0` fallback; it now exports an empty cell.
8. **Restricted-page detection** missed Chrome's "Cannot access …" error
   phrasings, so `chrome://` tabs showed the generic sleep message instead
   of the security explanation; the match now covers that family.
9. **Missing events**: `tabs.onActivated` and `windows.onFocusChanged` were
   not subscribed, so active-tab highlights and `lastAccessed` went stale
   until an unrelated event fired. Both added (the debounce + snapshot-skip
   absorb the extra firings).

## Affected files

- `components/Favicon.tsx` — new.
- `components/TabCard.tsx` — deleted (unused, contained the same bug).
- `components/TabListView.tsx` — uses `Favicon`; "—" for unknown times;
  once-a-minute clock tick.
- `components/PreviewPanel.tsx` — uses `Favicon`; per-tab wake/sleep state;
  guarded hostname parsing.
- `services/tabService.ts` — origin-scoped favicon cache; stable
  `lastAccessed` fallback; broader restricted-page detection; subscribes to
  `onActivated`/`onFocusChanged`.
- `App.tsx` — onboarding session guard; `loadTabsRef` stale-closure fix;
  snapshot-signature skip with `force` for manual refresh; authoritative
  name-map recompute; viewport-aware preview default; CSV export guard.

## Verified non-causes

For the record, the investigation explicitly ruled out: a feedback loop from
`loadTabs` itself; unstable React row keys; React resetting the DOM-mutated
`img.src` (React 18 diffs against its own previous vdom, not the live DOM);
CSP blocking favicons; `scrollIntoView` or CSS transitions replaying on
re-render; and sticky-header repaints.

## Out of scope

- Filtering which `chrome.tabs.onUpdated` payloads trigger a reload (the
  snapshot-signature skip makes this mostly moot).
- Persisting "welcome dismissed" across sessions on plain X-dismissal (the
  existing checkbox already provides permanence; see Issue 6 semantics).
- `table-fixed` column layout: considered as insurance against width
  redistribution, but measurement showed text columns are hard-capped by
  `truncate`, and fixed widths risk clipping. Revisit only if any residual
  jitter is observed after these fixes.
